lifeStatusEvidence.basis: Biographical sources listed below; this review adds no posthumous event as an activity by the subject.

changes: Added event-12 for 1912 Ministry of Education service and the move from Nanjing to Beijing.
Added event-13 for part-time university teaching from autumn 1920 and the lecture basis of A Brief History of Chinese Fiction.
Replaced Wikipedia source s4 with the independent Simon & Schuster author biography for the same birth/death cross-check. Added s5 by Chen Shuyu at the Academy of Chinese Studies.
editorialNotes: Xu Shoushang’s chronology, republished by the Chinese Writers Association, was read with the Peking University history museum, the Academy of Chinese Studies essay and Simon & Schuster author biography.
The chronology explicitly marks dates before 1912 as lunar; no lunar month was silently converted into a Gregorian month. The new entry uses year 1912 and its attested May move.
A university-hosted MCLC biography was found through indexed search but returned HTTP 502 twice. It was not substituted for the accessible full texts supporting the new entries.
The year 1920 applies to teaching, 1923 to the first volume and 1924 to the second volume of the fiction history; the existing 1923 entry remains correctly limited to volume one.
The subject died in 1936. No new life event after death is claimed, and the full range of his essays, translations and cultural work is not reduced to a complete bibliography claim.
This is an AI editorial and translation review; no human or native-speaker certification is asserted.
The existing stable item IDs, life status and rating fields are preserved. No influence rating is added. The chronology is selective, not a complete daily record.

translationReview.method: Existing validated canonical snapshots were checked before edits. Seven explicitly scoped delta exports/imports were reviewed; changed units were translated and checked by AI, shared facts were checked, and unchanged strings were reused. No hashes were edited directly.
